title: A Current for the Passage
premise: Felix Blackwood, a disgraced railroad engineer drowning in debt, accepts a dying prospector's map of a sunken salvage wreck in exchange for a promise: deliver it to the man's estranged daughter before the government concession permits expire in six tides. Pursued by the ruthless Meridian salvage fleet and shadowed by a marshal who wants the prospector's killer, Felix and the daughter, Isla, race down closed rail lines his old map lets him reopen. Betrayal within their small crew forces Felix to choose between loyalty to the friend who got him into this and the truth that could clear his name. In the end, Felix beats the fleet to the wreck by a single tide, surrenders the salvage rights to Isla as payment of his promise, and rides out with his debt paid in something better than money: a clean conscience.
about_author: Freya Thornbury is the pen name of a former surveyor's assistant who spent five years mapping abandoned rail corridors across the coastal ranges. She writes adventure fiction about people caught between what they owe and what they know.

chapters.title: The Dying Trade
chapters.summary: Felix Blackwood, hounded by creditors, is cornered by a bleeding prospector named Aldous Crane who trades him a wax-sealed map for a sworn promise to carry it to his daughter in Port Calloway. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: reluctant obligation — Felix takes the map not from honor but because a dying man leaves no room for refusal.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Felix learns the map marks a wreck inside a concession zone whose permits expire in six tides, after which the Meridian salvage fleet claims everything. He meets Isla Crane, who wants nothing to do with her father's legacy until she reads his letter. POV: Isla. Emotional beat: grief hardening into resolve as she agrees to go.

chapters.title: Closed Lines
chapters.summary: Felix uses his old railroad maps to route them along decommissioned lines, outrunning Meridian's agents at the first junction. A young drifter, Tam Wicks, stows away aboard their handcar and proves useful. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: the thrill of competence — his disgrace becomes an advantage for the first time in years.

chapters.title: The Marshal's Shadow
chapters.summary: Marshal Edith Vane catches up at a river crossing; she believes Crane was murdered and suspects Felix. She lets them pass on condition they send word if they find evidence. POV: Isla. Emotional beat: distrust — Isla wonders whether her father trusted the wrong man with his map.

chapters.title: What Tam Knew
chapters.summary: Tam reveals he worked for Meridian and was sent to track the map; he claims he fled rather than report them. That night someone signals their campfire location from a ridge. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: guilt and fear — Tam's divided loyalty begins to crack the crew's fragile trust.

chapters.title: The Washout
chapters.summary: A storm collapses a tunnel on the third tide, stranding them with Meridian's lead agent, Sorrel Dane, closing in. Felix engineers a risky detour over a trestle at flood stage, nearly losing Isla to the current. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into trust — Isla stops doubting him after he refuses to let go.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Ledger
chapters.summary: Felix discovers Tam has been feeding their position to Meridian to buy forgiveness for a debt of his own. Confronted, Tam confesses Crane's death was no accident — Dane killed him. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: shame and the terrible cost of survival, echoing the book's central theme.

chapters.title: The Fifth Tide
chapters.summary: With one tide to spare, they reach Port Calloway only to find Meridian's fleet already anchored off the wreck site, permits still valid until dawn. Marshal Vane arrives with warrants but no proof against Dane. POV: Isla. Emotional beat: despair sharpening into defiance — Isla proposes using the map's second annotation, which Felix never decoded.

chapters.title: Wreck of the Meridian Line
chapters.summary: The decoded annotation reveals a submerged rail cut leading under the fleet's anchorage. Felix pilots a borrowed launch through the cut at slack water; Tam sacrifices himself to jam the fleet's winch cable, forcing Dane's exposure. Vane arrests Dane with Tam's testimony recorded. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: climax — courage, loss, and justice achieved outside any courtroom.

chapters.title: A Current for the Passage
chapters.summary: At dawn on the sixth tide, Felix signs the salvage claim over to Isla, settling his promise though not his debts. Vane offers to help clear his name with the railroad board. Felix declines the escort home and takes the open line south — but this time, someone waves back. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — survival's price paid, truth chosen over easy loyalty, and a future unmoored but honest.
